by_judge.judge: C M POONACHA WILL SIT IN COURT HALL NO.6 AT DHARWAD

narrative:
On September 3, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 35.6%, taking up 849 of the 2,386 scheduled cases across 48 sitting judges. This represents a decline from prior recorded sittings, which registered 42.2% on August 28 (1,102 of 2,611 heard), 36.8% on August 14 (950 of 2,580 heard), and 44.5% on August 3 (1,103 of 2,478 heard). 

Workload and disposal varied substantially across court halls. Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty addressed the largest individual volume, hearing 89 of 191 listed cases (46.6%). Substantial progress was also recorded by Justice V. Srishananda, who heard 47 of 74 matters (63.5%), and Justice Venkatesh Naik T, who disposed of 48 out of 93 matters across his lists. Conversely, high-volume dockets before Justice M. Nagaprasanna (95 cases), Justice S. Rachaiah (49 cases), and Justice M.I. Arun (41 cases) concluded without any matters heard.

Procedural stages heavily dictated throughput. Interlocutory and procedural orders formed the bulk of the docket, with 350 of 843 matters heard (41.5%), tracking lower than the 45.4% conversion seen on August 28. Admission stages converted 137 of 321 cases (42.7%). Final hearing matters achieved a 22.8% conversion rate (114 of 501 heard), outperforming rates from August 14 (17.7%) and August 3 (16.5%), though trailing August 28 (25.1%). Preliminary hearings saw a modest clearance of 24.7% (89 of 361).

By case type, Writ Petitions (WP) represented the largest caseload, with 346 of 1,103 cases heard (31.4%), reflecting a lower clearance than the 39.6% and 44.8% recorded in late August and early August. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) saw 126 of 299 matters heard (42.1%), while Regular Second Appeals (RSA) achieved a 50.4% hearing rate (68 of 135). In contrast, Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) converted only 26.0% (47 of 181), dropping markedly from the 44.0% clearance observed on August 28.
